verses.1:1: The burden that Habakkuk the prophet beheld.
verses.1:2: How long, O LORD, have I cried for help, and You do not hear? I cry out to You, "Violence!" and You do not save.
verses.1:3: Why do You make me see iniquity, and look upon trouble? Destruction and violence are before me; there is strife, and contention rises up.
verses.1:4: Therefore the law grows numb, and justice never comes forth; for the wicked hems in the righteous, therefore judgment comes forth perverted.
verses.1:5: Look among the nations and watch; be astounded and amazed! For I am performing a work in your days that you would not believe, even if it were recounted.
verses.1:6: For behold, I am raising up the Chaldeans, that bitter and impetuous nation, which marches through the broad expanse of the earth to possess dwellings that are not its own.
verses.1:7: They are dreadful and fearsome; their justice and dignity proceed from themselves.
verses.1:8: Their horses are swifter than leopards and fiercer than wolves of the evening; their horsemen charge forth, and their horsemen come from afar; they swoop like an eagle hastening to devour.
verses.1:9: All of them come for violence; the thrust of their faces presses eagerly forward, and they gather captives like the sand.
verses.1:10: They scoff at kings, and rulers are a laughingstock to them; they laugh at every fortress, for they heap up earthen mounds and capture it.
verses.1:11: Then they sweep by like the wind and pass through, becoming guilty—they whose own might is their god.
verses.1:12: Are You not from of old, O LORD my God, my Holy One? We shall not die. O LORD, You have appointed them for judgment; and O Rock, You have established them for correction.
verses.1:13: Your eyes are too pure to behold evil, and You cannot look upon wrongdoing; why then do You look on the treacherous, and keep silent when the wicked swallows up one more righteous than he?
verses.1:14: You make mankind like the fish of the sea, like creeping things that have no ruler over them.
verses.1:15: He brings all of them up with a hook; he drags them away in his net and gathers them into his dragnet; therefore he rejoices and exults.
verses.1:16: Therefore he sacrifices to his net and burns incense to his dragnet, for through them his portion is rich and his food is sumptuous.
verses.1:17: Shall he therefore keep emptying his net, and continually slay the nations without sparing?
verses.2:1: I will take my stand at my watchpost and station myself upon the rampart; I will keep watch to see what He will speak to me, and what I shall answer concerning my complaint.
verses.2:2: Then the LORD answered me and said, "Write down the vision and make it plain upon the tablets, so that one who reads it may run.
verses.2:3: For the vision is still for the appointed time; it hastens toward the end and will not prove false. Though it lingers, wait for it; for it shall surely come, it shall not delay."
verses.2:4: Behold, his soul is puffed up and is not upright within him; yet the righteous man shall live by his faith.
verses.2:5: Moreover, wine is a betrayer; an arrogant man does not abide at rest. He widens his appetite like Sheol, and like death he is never satisfied; he gathers to himself all the nations and assembles for himself all the peoples.
verses.2:6: Shall not all these take up a taunt against him, with derisive riddles aimed at him, and say, "Woe to him who piles up what is not his own—how long?—and weighs himself down with pledges!
verses.2:7: Shall not your creditors suddenly rise up, and those who make you tremble awake? Then you shall become plunder for them.
verses.2:8: Because you have plundered many nations, all the remnant of the peoples shall plunder you, on account of human bloodshed and violence done to the land, to the city, and to all who dwell in it.
verses.2:9: Woe to him who gains unjust profit for his house, that he may set his nest on high and be delivered from the grasp of calamity!
verses.2:10: You have plotted shame for your house by cutting off many peoples, and you have sinned against your own soul.
verses.2:11: For the stone shall cry out from the wall, and the beam from the timber shall answer it.
verses.2:12: Woe to him who builds a town with bloodshed and establishes a city by iniquity!
verses.2:13: Behold, is it not from the LORD of hosts that the peoples labor only for the fire, and the nations weary themselves for emptiness?
verses.2:14: For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the LORD's glory, even as the waters overspread the sea.
verses.2:15: Woe to him who gives his neighbor drink, pouring out your venom and making him drunk as well, so as to gaze upon their nakedness!
verses.2:16: You are sated with disgrace instead of honor; drink, you too, and show your uncircumcision! The cup of the LORD's right hand shall come around to you, and utter disgrace shall come upon your glory.
verses.2:17: For the violence done to Lebanon shall overwhelm you, and the destruction of the beasts that terrified them, on account of human bloodshed and violence done to the land, to the city, and to all who dwell in it.
verses.2:18: What profit is a carved image when its maker has shaped it—a cast metal image, a teacher of falsehood? For the craftsman trusts in his own handiwork when he fashions speechless idols.
verses.2:19: Woe to him who says to wood, 'Awake!' and to a silent stone, 'Arise!' Can it give instruction? Behold, it is overlaid with gold and silver, yet there is no breath at all within it."
verses.2:20: But the LORD is in His holy temple; be hushed before Him, all the earth!
verses.3:1: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, set to Shigionoth.
verses.3:2: O LORD, I have heard the report of You, and I fear; O LORD, bring Your work to life in the midst of the years; in the midst of the years make it known; in wrath, remember mercy.
verses.3:3: God comes from Teman, and the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah. His majesty overspreads the heavens, and His praise fills the earth.
verses.3:4: His radiance is like the daylight; rays flash from His hand, and there is the hiding place of His might.
verses.3:5: Pestilence marches before Him, and plague goes forth at His feet.
verses.3:6: He stood and measured the earth; He looked and startled the nations. The everlasting mountains were shattered; the ancient hills bowed down. His ways are everlasting.
verses.3:7: I saw the tents of Cushan in distress; the curtains of the land of Midian trembled.
verses.3:8: Was Your indignation against the rivers, O LORD? Was Your anger against the rivers, or Your fury against the sea, that You rode upon Your horses, upon Your chariots of salvation?
verses.3:9: You laid bare Your bow; oaths were sworn over the shafts of Your word. Selah. You cleaved the earth with rivers.
verses.3:10: The mountains saw You and writhed; a torrent of waters swept by. The deep uttered its voice and lifted its hands on high.
verses.3:11: The sun and moon stood still in their lofty abode at the light of Your arrows as they sped, at the gleam of Your glittering spear.
verses.3:12: In indignation You marched through the earth; in anger You threshed the nations.
verses.3:13: You went forth for the deliverance of Your people, for the deliverance of Your anointed; You crushed the head from the house of the wicked, laying it bare from foundation to neck. Selah.
verses.3:14: You pierced with his own shafts the head of his warriors; they stormed out like a whirlwind to scatter me, their exultation like that of those who devour the afflicted in secret.
verses.3:15: You trampled the sea with Your horses, the surging heap of mighty waters.
verses.3:16: I heard, and my inward parts trembled; my lips quivered at the sound. Rottenness entered into my bones, and I shook beneath myself, yet I will wait quietly for the day of distress to come upon the people who invade us.
verses.3:17: Though the fig tree does not bud, and no yield is on the vines; though the produce of the olive fails, and the terraced fields produce no food; though the flock is cut off from the fold, and no cattle are in the stalls—
verses.3:18: yet I will exult in the LORD; I will rejoice in the God of my salvation.
verses.3:19: GOD the Lord is my strength; He makes my feet like the feet of deer, and causes me to tread upon my high places. For the choirmaster, with my stringed instruments.

notes.1:1: Hebrew massa carries the dual sense of "burden" and "prophetic oracle," conveying the weighty gravity of the message.
notes.1:9: The rare Hebrew noun megammat occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible and denotes an eager thrust or sweeping horde pressing forward.
notes.1:12: The Masoretic text reads "We shall not die," translated here as written; rabbinic tradition notes this verse among the tiqqun soferim, suggesting an original reading "You shall not die."
notes.2:4: Hebrew emunah encompasses both steadfast faith and loyal faithfulness, standing in sharp contrast to the puffed-up soul of the arrogant oppressor.
notes.2:6: Hebrew avtit denotes pledges or heavy debts accumulated through extortionate lending.
notes.2:16: The Masoretic text reads "show your uncircumcision," an image of utter disgrace; several ancient witnesses reflect a transposed consonant meaning "stagger."
notes.2:17: The Masoretic verbal form yechitan is grammatically unusual and is rendered here as "that terrified them," referring to the havoc inflicted on Lebanon's wildlife.
notes.3:1: Shigionoth is an uncertain musical or liturgical term, likely denoting a passionate, heightened poetic style (cf. Psalm 7:1).
notes.3:9: The three-word Hebrew clause literally containing "oaths," "rods/shafts," and "word" is a celebrated crux, expressing the divinely sworn decree behind God's weapons of judgment.
notes.3:19: The Masoretic order of the divine names here is rendered "GOD the Lord," and the final musical subscription dedicates the prophet's prayer for liturgical performance.
